title: Labeling and fixation of lysosomes in living eukaryotic cells
author: Scerra, Caporaso, et al.
materials: In this section we describe in detail the setting and acquisition mode applicable to either living or fixed cells by using the Ultraview VoX spinning disk system (PerkinElmer) (D'Agostino et al., 2018; D'Agostino et al., 2017; D'Agostino et al., 2016) or the LSM700 confocal system (Carl Zeiss) (D'Agostino et al., 2014; D'Agostino et al., 2013), respectively. The protocol described here is applicable for any fluorescent molecule excitable at 488 nm (such as a GFP, FITC, Alexa Fluor 488, etc.), as well as for other fluorescent molecules excitable at any other different wavelengths.9.Live-imaging acquisition procedure:This section of the protocol describes the visualization of the exogenous lysosomal marker Lamp1-mGFP protein. For the live-based visualization, cells must be grown in multi-well with glass-bottom and the microscope must be equipped with a dedicated chamber necessary to maintain temperature and CO2 at 37°C and 5%, respectively.a.Switch on the microscope and set up parameters to the thermostatic chamber to let it reach the selected temperature and CO2.b.All samples are observed by using an oil immersion objective (63× 1.4 NA).c.The channel is set to 488-nm laser by using the Ultraview VoX spinning disk software.d.Adjust the laser power and time exposure. For this study, the variables were adjusted as follows: laser power at 50% and time exposure between 200 and 500 ms.e.Researchers should optimize the settings for optimal image intensity.f.After capturing, images can be processed using the Ultraview VoX spinning disk software to adjust their intensity.g.Capture images from at least 20 different fields for the quantification of lysosomal diameter.h.Acquired images are saved as .Tiff, .JPG or .PNG formats and can be visualized for quantitative analysis by using the ImageJ Fiji software.10.Acquisition procedure from fixed cells:This section describes the visualization of stained cells to analyze the endogenous lysosomal marker Lamp1 protein. All images are acquired by confocal microscopy. To use LSM700 software, researchers need to refer to the manufacturer’s manual for the Zeiss LSM700 instrument.a.All samples are observed using a confocal microscope equipped with a 63× or 40× 1.4 NA oil immersion objective. The observation can be made even with a non-confocal microscope.CRITICAL: Do not use non-oil objectives. The oil is necessary to improve the resolving power of the microscope which is crucial to get high-resolution images that allow the best estimation of the dimension from the smallest to the largest lysosomal structures.b.The channel is set to 488-nm laser by using the LSM700 Zeiss software.c.Adjust the pinhole, laser power, PMT gain, and offset. For this study, the variables were adjusted as follows: pinhole at 0,42 A.U., laser power at 2.0, PMT gain between 500 and 700, and the offset at −20.d.Researchers should optimize the settings for optimal image intensity varying and keeping laser power or PMT gain always under the maximum before bleaching. Anyway, the instructions we have provided on the Lamp1-mGFP expressing cells, the antibody against Lamp1, and the fixation procedures guarantee the optimal outcome which can be easily reached also with other acquisition systems including the non-confocal ones.e.After capturing, images can be processed using LSM700 Zeiss software to adjust their intensity.f.Capture images from at least 20 different fields of three independent experiments. For a good statistically significant quantification, one need to analyze at least 50 lysosomal diameters for 20 cells/experiment for a total of 3000 lysosomal diameters.g.Acquired images are saved as “.lsm5” format and can be opened using LSM700 or ImageJ Fiji software. Images can then be exported to the .Tiff, .JPG, .PNG, and many others for the post-processing analysis.

steps.title: Prepare and plate cells on coverslips
steps.instruction: Seed Lamp1‑mGFP HeLa cells onto sterile glass coverslips to reach ~50 % confluency after 16 h incubation.

substeps.instruction: Trypsinize exponentially growing cells (passage 3‑20): remove medium, wash once with pre‑warmed PBS, add trypsin (or any detaching solution), incubate until cells are single‑cell; resuspend in medium, centrifuge gently, aspirate trypsin.
Resuspend the pellet in an appropriate volume of culture medium to obtain the desired cell density.

Prepare coverslips: if not clean, wash with 1 % SDS, rinse extensively with deionized water; if not sterile, sterilize at 200 °C for 2 h. Wash once with 1× PBS. Using sterile forceps, place round 10 mm coverslips (24‑well) or 13 mm coverslips (12‑well) at the bottom of the well and gently press to ensure adhesion.
Optional: coat coverslips with an adhesion agent suitable for HeLa cells.
Seed cells onto the coverslips to achieve ~50 % confluency; spread the plate in multiple directions to avoid cell clusters; gently push the coverslip to the bottom of the well with a sterile tip.
Incubate plates in a humidified incubator at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 16 h.

steps.title: Treat cells with amino‑acid analogs
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with 1–10 mM amino‑acid methyl‑ester analogs for at least 2 h to expand lysosomes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a working solution by diluting the chosen amino‑acid analog stock (L‑Leucine‑ME·HCl, L‑Alanine‑ME·HCl, or L‑Histidine‑ME·HCl) in culture medium to the desired concentration (1 mM for mild expansion, up to 10 mM for maximal expansion).
Remove the existing culture medium from the cells (step 6b).
Add the medium containing the amino‑acid analogs (step 6c) without any additional starvation step.
Return the plate to the incubator (37 °C, 5 % CO₂) for 2 h.
If phenol‑red‑containing medium is used, expect a yellow colour change because the analogs are slightly acidic.

steps.title: Immunostain endogenous Lamp1 (fixed cells)
steps.instruction: Permeabilize, block, and label fixed cells with primary and secondary antibodies, then mount for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: If cells were fixed with methanol, skip permeabilization; otherwise, permeabilize by incubating cells in blocking buffer (0.05 % saponin, 1 % BSA in 1× PBS) for 15 min at room temperature (RT).
Prepare primary antibody solution: dilute anti‑Lamp1 antibody 1:500 in blocking buffer.
Wash cells once with 1× PBS at 25 °C.
Mix the diluted primary antibody by inversion or vortexing, then spin down briefly.
Place a rectangle of parafilm on the bench and wet its edges with a few drops of water so it adheres to the surface.
Add 50 µL of the primary antibody solution onto the parafilm (sufficient for 10 mm or 13 mm coverslips).
Remove excess PBS from the coverslip by touching it to adsorbing paper, then invert the coverslip (cells‑down) onto the drop and incubate 1 h at RT.
After incubation, add 150 µL of 1× PBS between the parafilm and the coverslip to keep the coverslip floating.
Wash the coverslip three times with 1× PBS, 5 min each wash.
Prepare secondary antibody solution: dilute Alexa Fluor 488‑conjugated secondary antibody 1:500 in blocking buffer; mix and spin down briefly.
Add 50 µL drops of the secondary antibody onto parafilm, place the coverslip (cell side down) onto the drop, and incubate 45 min at RT in the dark (cover with a lid to prevent photobleaching).
Wash the coverslip three times with 1× PBS, 5 min each wash.
Add 10 µL of mounting solution onto a microscope slide.
Dip the coverslip briefly in sterile water to remove residual salts, then place it onto the mounting drop.
Allow the slide to dry in a dark chamber before imaging.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence images of live or fixed cells using appropriate microscope settings.

substeps.instruction: Live‑cell imaging:
a. Place the multi‑well plate with glass‑bottom into a microscope chamber set to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
b. Use a 63× 1.4 NA oil‑immersion objective.
c. Select the 488‑nm laser channel (Ultraview VoX spinning‑disk software).
d. Set laser power to 50 % and exposure time between 200–500 ms (adjust as needed).
e. Optimize settings for adequate intensity without bleaching.
f. Capture images from at least 20 different fields; save as .tif, .jpg or .png.
Fixed‑cell imaging:
a. Use a confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM700 or equivalent) with a 63× or 40× 1.4 NA oil‑immersion objective (oil required).
b. Select the 488‑nm laser channel.
c. Set pinhole to 0.42 A.U., laser power to 2.0, PMT gain to 500–700, offset to –20 (adjust as needed).
d. Optimize settings to avoid bleaching.
e. Capture images from at least 20 fields per experiment; acquire at least 50 lysosomal diameters from 20 cells in each of three independent experiments (≈3000 measurements total).
f. Save files as .lsm5 (or .lsm7) and optionally export to .tif, .jpg, .png for analysis.

steps.title: Quantify lysosomal diameter
steps.instruction: Measure lysosomal diameters in Fiji/ImageJ and perform statistical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Open the exported image file in Fiji.
Select the straight line tool and draw a line across the diameter of each enlarged lysosome using the Lamp1 fluorescence as the membrane reference.
If necessary, zoom the image to improve visibility of the fluorescent signal.
Measure the line (Analyze → Measure) to obtain length in pixels.
Repeat for 50 lysosomes per 20 cells in each of three independent experiments (≈3000 measurements).
Measure the 20 µm scale bar in the same image to obtain the pixel‑to‑µm conversion factor.
Convert each diameter to µm using: (diameter pixels / scale‑bar pixels) × 20 µm.
Compile the converted values, calculate mean and standard deviation, and plot a histogram.
Assess statistical significance with One‑way ANOVA.
